---
title: "Scope & non-goals"
description: "What EOS Reimagined promises, what it deliberately does not, and where it stands on piracy and cheating."
---

## What this is

EOS Reimagined keeps games playable after their backend is gone. It is a reverse-engineered,
from-scratch, GPL-3.0 stand-in for the EOS SDK's shared library that answers the SDK's calls
locally and connects players **directly to each other** over the local network. The intended
uses are exactly these:

- **LAN parties for disserviced games** — a title whose EOS-backed multiplayer went dark still
  has working netcode; this gives it peers again.
- **Couch co-op and splitscreen that was never shipped** — several local copies of one game,
  each its own player, meshing on one machine or one living room.
- **Preservation** — multiplayer that does not depend on any company's continued interest.

This is our contribution to the goals of [Stop Killing Games](https://www.stopkillinggames.com/).
Communities like [SplitScreen.me](https://splitscreen.me),
[Nucleus Co-op](https://nucleus-coop.github.io) and
[PartyDeck](https://github.com/partydeck/partydeck) do adjacent, excellent work — EOS Reimagined
is the piece that answers the SDK.

## A statement on feature parity

EOS Reimagined is a reverse-engineered stand-in, **not a certified replacement**, and we cannot
guarantee one-to-one behavior with Epic's SDK. True parity would mean rebuilding Epic's entire
backend — matchmaking, voice relays, anti-cheat — which we have not done and may never fully do.
What exists today is the part that keeps games playable: identity, sessions, lobbies, presence,
peer-to-peer messaging, and the social surface, wired over an authenticated LAN mesh, plus an
honest compatibility shell where a real service cannot exist (see the
[roadmap](roadmap.qmd) for the exact ledger). Two limitations deserve to be called out up front:

**1. It authenticates keys, not accounts — and does no anti-cheat.**
The transport is genuinely secure: every connection runs a Noise XX handshake, every frame is
sealed, and a peer's identity is derived from the key it *proved* rather than anything it claims
— a forged, tampered, or replayed message simply does not open
([the full design](../developers/internals/adr/0001-authenticated-mesh-identity.qmd)). What that cannot do is
attest a real Epic account or game ownership; that would require Epic, and we do not pretend to
it. Likewise we implement none of Epic Anti-Cheat: a game that leans entirely on EAC for
integrity gets no protection from this library, so a modified client is easier to run than it
would be on Epic's backend unless the game enforces its own checks. Neither gap is fixable
without a trusted backend, and we say so rather than fake it.

**2. It does not talk to Epic.**
The emulator speaks its own reconstructed peer-to-peer protocol between copies of *itself*. It
never connects to Epic's servers, and we neither expect nor intend that someone running EOS
Reimagined can matchmake with someone on the genuine SDK against Epic's live backend. This is a
tool for connecting emulator to emulator — not emulator to Epic.

## A statement on piracy and cheating

**This tool is for keeping games playable. We will *never* support players who wish to use EOS
Reimagined to play on cracked copies of games or develop cheats.**

This project shall *only* be used to facilitate splitscreen, couch co-op, or continued
multiplayer for games that are dying or dead — LAN parties for a game whose servers went dark,
two local copies seeing each other for co-op the developer never shipped. It is expected that you
own legitimate copies of the games you play. It follows that we do **not** intend to support
letting pirated copies slip onto official servers or play alongside legitimate owners — which the
architecture already precludes: nothing here can reach Epic's services at all.

Issues and pull requests whose purpose is piracy convenience or cheat development will be closed.

## Permanent non-goals

| Non-goal | Why |
|---|---|
| Interoperating with Epic's live backend | Different trust root, different servers, and deliberately so. |
| Attesting accounts or ownership | Impossible without Epic; claiming it would be a lie. |
| Anti-cheat, or anti-cheat bypass | We implement neither Epic's anti-cheat nor tools to defeat it. |
| Being a piracy vector | See above — and the design gives it nothing to connect to. |

## Deferred, not refused

LAN-only discovery (Internet traversal is future work), voice transport, overlay rendering, and
platform-native invite UIs are all *scheduling* decisions, revisited as the project matures —
the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) tracks each with its reasons.
